name: CV / Resume Analysis - Frontend Developer
description: Signals extracted from the user's CV/resume to evidence Frontend Developer skills. CV data provides self-reported information that must be cross-validated with GitHub and assessment sources.

extraction_rules.description: How to extract and weight information from CV content for Frontend roles.

sections.description: Explicit list of technologies and tools mentioned in skills section.
sections.notes: Low strength because listing a skill doesn't prove proficiency. 'React' in a skills list alone is insufficient — must cross-reference with projects and experience.

sections.description: Job descriptions and responsibilities mentioning frontend development activities.
sections.notes: Higher strength when specific actions and outcomes are described.
quality_indicators: Specific frameworks and versions mentioned in context (e.g., 'migrated from CRA to Vite' not just 'used React')
Quantifiable outcomes (improved LCP by 40%, reduced bundle size by 60%)
Action verbs indicating hands-on work (architected, implemented, optimized, migrated, refactored)
Duration and recency of frontend-specific experience

sections.description: Personal or professional projects demonstrating frontend skills.
sections.notes: Higher strength if linked to GitHub repository or live demo. Cross-reference with GitHub analysis.
quality_indicators: Technical depth of project description (e.g., 'built a real-time dashboard with WebSocket and virtual scrolling')
Links to source code, live demo, or Storybook
Complexity indicators (SSR, state management, accessibility compliance)

sections.description: Relevant courses, degrees, and bootcamp certificates.
sections.notes: Provides context but doesn't directly evidence practical frontend skill. Relevant for career changers and bootcamp grads.

sections.description: Professional certifications relevant to frontend development.
sections.notes: Frontend certifications are less standardized than cloud/infra certs. They indicate theoretical knowledge but not practical build skill.

frontend_specific: freeCodeCamp JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures
web_general: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (frontend deployment context)
accessibility: IAAP CPACC (Certified Professional in Accessibility Core Competencies)

signal_mapping.description: How CV mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: Describes building React/Vue SPA with specific component architecture
Lists React or Vue in skills section only
Describes building CI/CD pipeline for frontend with preview deploys
Mentions Next.js SSR/SSG with performance metrics
Improved Core Web Vitals or Lighthouse scores with quantified results
Implemented design system or component library
Wrote comprehensive test suites with high coverage
Has Meta Front-End Developer or freeCodeCamp certification without project evidence

important_notes: CV data is self-reported and inherently unreliable as standalone evidence
Always cross-validate CV claims with GitHub and assessment data
Frontend certifications alone are NOT evidence of practical skill — frontend is learned by building
Look for specificity and depth — 'used React' is weaker than 'migrated class components to hooks and reduced re-renders by 40%'
Recency matters — jQuery expertise from 2015 without modern framework experience is a concern
Quantifiable performance improvements (LCP, bundle size, test coverage) are strong signals
